title: Measures to Help Police Protect Public and Guide Individuals at risk of Being Drawn into Knife-related Crimes
what_it_is: Measures to Help Police Protect Public and Guide Individuals at risk of Being Drawn into Knife-related Crimes

sections.label: Knife-related crime statistics
sections.summary: Knife-related crimes involving murder, robbery, rioting and serious hurt averaged about 150 cases annually over five years, with 36% in residential areas and 3% in educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In the past five years, the number of knife-related crimes involving murder, robbery, rioting and serious hurt has remained relatively constant, averaging about 150 cases annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: About 36% of these crimes occurred in residential areas and 3% happened in educational institution premises.

sections.label: Regulated weapons under AEA
sections.summary: MHA regulates six items under the Arms and Explosives Act, and the list will expand to include knuckledusters and flick knives when the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act replaces it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: MHA, currently, regulates six items under the Arms and Explosives Act, or AEA – sword, spear, spearhead, dagger, bayonet and dangerous bows and arrows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: This list of regulated weapons will be expanded to include items, such as knuckledusters and flick knives, when the Guns, Explosives and Weapons Control Act replaces the AEA later this year.

sections.label: Mandatory treatment order
sections.summary: The MTO would compel a person to undergo psychiatric treatment for up to 36 months instead of imprisonment, facilitating rehabilitation and treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The MTO would compel the person to undergo psychiatric treatment for up to 36 months in lieu of imprisonment, which would facilitate the rehabilitation and treatment of the individual involved.

sections.label: Mobile self-help stations
sections.summary: Mobile self-help stations, Police Beacons, have been deployed in secluded areas such as the Punggol Park Connector area where the public can activate the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: In addition to that, we have actually deployed in some areas – where we think they may be more secluded – some mobile self-help stations, Police Beacons, where members of the public can activate the Police at the locations, for example, in the Punggol Park Connector area.

sections.label: Increased police patrols
sections.summary: The Police will continue to increase patrols in potential high-crime areas with more public reports, to give better assurance to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The Police will continue to increase patrols in areas where there is potential high crime, where we have received more reports from members of the public, to give better assurance to members of the public as well.

sections.label: Rehabilitative programmes and mental health
sections.summary: Prison services have rehabilitative programmes for those at risk of violent re-offending, and MHA works with mental health agencies to address public concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: The first part on SPS, I have mentioned briefly in my speech that the prison services today already have existing rehabilitative programmes for those who are at risk of violent re-offending and these include teaching them how to manage their own emotions and how do they deal with the urge to take offensive actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: For other members of the public or people who are looking for help, there are more than just the prison service, the Police or MHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We are working with other agencies which are dealing with mental health and mental issues to help address the concerns of some members of the public.
